metrics.name: Conversation MCP Use
metrics.reason: The score is 0.95 because the application largely met the evaluation criteria: it gathered requirements, used appropriate workload and traffic tools with valid arguments, confirmed the 50-user workload, applied the correct A100-80 hardware filter, and made targeted calls to resolve duplicate recommendations. It also appropriately requested GPU details when the cluster resource tool was unavailable and stopped at the selection handoff without deploying. Minor parameter inaccuracies prevented a perfect score: the minimum quality threshold was set to 32 instead of the required integer threshold of 33, and the cost ceiling was rounded to $1,789 instead of $1,788.50.

metrics.name: Conversation MCP Task Completion
metrics.reason: The score is 0.8 because the application clarified requirements, presented workload targets and hardware-filtered recommendations, and delivered the selected-model handoff without attempting deployment. However, it incorrectly used peak traffic of 0.13 req/s instead of the displayed expected traffic of 0.07 req/s in the handoff and downplayed a substantial end-to-end latency difference despite speed being the user's priority. These errors prevented full credit; no explicit pass or fail status was provided.

metrics.name: Navigator Skill Fidelity [Conversational GEval]
metrics.reason: The navigator skill is present and largely followed: all three phases are announced, the assistant waits for workload confirmation before recommendations, asks about unavailable GPU inventory and waits for the A100-80 answer, and obtains the model choice before handing off to /navigator-deploy without planning or executing deployment. Results use readable prose and markdown tables. Minor specification errors remain: the handoff uses peak traffic (0.13) rather than expected traffic (0.07) for expected_qps, and missing recommendation slots are explained without offering the required constraint-relaxation choice. The required pre-flight tool check is not demonstrated.

metrics.name: Conversation MCP Use
metrics.reason: The score is 0.9 because the application largely completed the selection-only task correctly, using appropriate tools, obtaining confirmed GPU details when resource discovery was unavailable, and supplying correctly typed arguments for 50 users, A100-80 hardware, and latency priority without invoking deployment tools. Targeted reruns addressed duplicate recommendations, but minor constraint errors reduced precision: the cost ceiling was rounded to $1,789 instead of $1,788.50, and the minimum quality was set to 32 rather than 33, which was needed to guarantee at least a five-point increase from 27.1.

metrics.name: Conversation MCP Task Completion
metrics.reason: The score is 0.8 because the application confirmed the workload, presented recommendations, obtained the user's balanced-model selection, and delivered the required handoff without attempting deployment. However, the handoff incorrectly set expected_qps to 0.13, using the peak rate instead of the stated expected traffic of 0.07 requests per second, so the task was not fully accurate.

metrics.name: Navigator Skill Fidelity [Conversational GEval]
metrics.reason: The navigator skill is present, and the assistant announced all three phases, waited for workload confirmation before recommendations, asked for GPU inventory and waited before filtering to A100-80, and waited for model selection before handing off to /navigator-deploy without planning or executing deployment. Results used readable prose and markdown tables. Minor specification errors remain: the handoff uses peak traffic (0.13) instead of expected traffic (0.07) for expected_qps, missing recommendation slots did not trigger an offer to relax constraints, and the cost explanation overstates what the tighter $1,789 search established.
